title: fix(sdui-parser): a registration's declared every-node member wins with its type in the generated JSX types, so the .d.ts over the public manifest compiles (objectui#11075)
body:
Fixes #11075
Clause-②: yes

## What this changes

`generateDts` now omits from `SduiBaseProps` every base attribute an interface's registration declares, whatever the member's scope. The declared input wins with its type. Before, objectui#11044 applied the `Omit` form only to the six `where-undeclared` members. An `every-node` member that a registration declares wider than the base type then conflicted with it:

`TS2430 Interface 'RecordAlertProps' incorrectly extends interface 'SduiBaseProps'`. `record:alert` declares `visible` as `boolean | string | object` (objectui#9100), and `SduiBaseProps.visible` is `boolean`.

Route 1, as triage `5888889628` ruled. `SduiBaseProps` itself is unchanged: `visible`, `disabled` and `hidden` stay `boolean` wherever a type does not declare them, so route 2 is not taken. `validate.ts` is untouched, so no `validateTree` verdict moves.

Generic type arguments are written in words below (for example, "`SduiBaseProps` with `visible` omitted"), because GitHub strips angle-bracket shapes from saved bodies.

## Measured on the real public manifest (objectui `origin/main` `3e71a9825`)

The manifest was built the way `dev/manifest-dump.tsx` builds `sdui.manifest.json`: the console's `register-plugins`, `@object-ui/components` and the dump's 15 eager plugin imports, with `assertFullyLoaded` passing. It has 107 types. `generateDts` over it was then compiled in memory with `strict` on, `skipLibCheck` unset and `types` empty.

- **Base:** 1 diagnostic, the TS2430 above.
- **This branch:** 0 diagnostics. The new pin re-derives this reading on every run.

These are the declared every-node members that reach the `.d.ts`. The census was measured once at the base and is not re-derived by any pin:

| member | declared on | declared type vs the base type |
|---|---|---|
| `visible` | 1 (`record:alert`) | `boolean`, `string` and `object`, wider than `boolean`: the one conflict |
| `disabled` | 1 (`element:button`) | `boolean`, the same |
| `className` | 67 | `string` on every one, the same |
| `children` | 56 | `slot` only on every one: no attribute is emitted, so nothing is omitted |
| `id`, `hidden`, the rest | 0 | none |

The dispatch's 519-type census was taken over the whole registry. The public manifest is the 107 types above.

**The one rule, applied to `className` as well:** the dispatch asked for a stop if the rule was wrong for a member. It is not wrong for `className`. Every one of the 67 declarations is `string`, so omitting it and redeclaring it types the same attribute the same way. The effect is textual. Over the real manifest, 69 interface headers change and no other line of the `.d.ts` does. Interfaces that extend `SduiBaseProps` with members omitted go from 20 to 78, and those that extend it plain go from 87 to 29. A conflicts-only rule would have to decide assignability from type strings inside the codegen. The code comment on `emitInterface` names that as the reason the rule has no per-key exception.

## Pins

- **New, real manifest:** `apps/console/src/__tests__/sdui-intrinsics-compile-11075.test.ts`. The test runs `dev/manifest-dump.tsx` itself instead of mirroring its imports. It reads the manifest the dump publishes and runs `generateDts` over it, as `buildArtifacts` does. It then type-checks that file plus a six-line page in memory with PR objectui#11072's harness, and asserts:
  - the generated file draws zero diagnostics;
  - `RecordAlertProps` extends `SduiBaseProps` with `visible` omitted, and `SduiBaseProps.visible` is still `boolean`;
  - on the page, `record:alert` takes `visible` as `true`, as a bare CEL string and as the `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` envelope, and refuses `42`;
  - control: `record:details`, which declares no `visible`, takes `true` and refuses a string.
- **Extended, synthetic manifest:** the objectui#11044 pin in `packages/sdui-parser` gains a `notice` type. It declares `visible` with the same three arms, `disabled` and `className` with the base types, and `children` as a slot. The pin asserts that `notice` omits exactly those three from the base, in declaration order, and keeps the base `children`. Five page cases are added: string, envelope, a refused number, the base `boolean` refusing a string on an undeclaring type, and slot children.
- **Text pins updated for the new clause:** these tests matched the old `extends` text of a type that declares `className`. In `packages/sdui-parser`, `html-tier-manifest-10735.test.ts` matches `AProps`. In `apps/console`, `html-tier-manifest.test.ts` matches `AProps`. In `packages/plugin-dashboard`, `dashboardAuthoredInputs.test.tsx` has the `DashboardProps` regex that the dispatch names in its gate list. That regex now expects `className` after `label` and `description`.

## Ablation (fix committed first, then the pre-fix rule restored)

The mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs`. It added the old `scope === 'where-undeclared'` condition back to the `BASE_ATTRIBUTES` filter in `emitInterface`: anchor count 1 to 0, blob `f6727b7c9f83` to `361c4746755e`. It then ran the two pin files.

- **Result: `4 failed | 65 passed (69)`.** The failures are the two file-level compile assertions (TS2430 on `RecordAlertProps` over the real manifest and on `NoticeProps` over the synthetic one) and the two assertions on the omitted text.
- **Observed direction:** the page-level JSX cases stayed green under the mutation. `tsc` still types a conflicting member by the derived interface's own declaration. A page check therefore cannot see this defect, and the file-level diagnostic assertion is the one that catches it.
- **Restore:** the blob matches HEAD (`f6727b7c9f83`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **No build was needed for this ablation.** The synthetic pin imports `../index.js`. The console project aliases `@object-ui/sdui-parser` to `packages/sdui-parser/src` in `apps/console/vite.config.ts`.

## Gates (all at HEAD `28e5fdfdc`)

- **vitest:** `pnpm exec vitest run` over `packages/sdui-parser/`, the three console manifest tests (the new one, `html-tier-manifest`, `element-data-source-input-injection`), `dashboardAuthoredInputs` and the components-side `base-props-one-list-11044`: `Test Files 25 passed (25)`, `Tests 363 passed (363)`.
- **Build:** `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/sdui-parser...' build` (the package and its 6 workspace dependencies) exited 0.
- **sdui-parser type-check:** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/sdui-parser type-check` exited 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists 20 test files, including both edited ones.
- **Console:** a type-check of the new test file alone, under `apps/console/tsconfig.json`'s options, drew 0 diagnostics in that file. The lit control, a file assigning `generateDts` to a `number`, drew 1 (TS2322).
- **eslint:** `pnpm exec eslint --format json` over the 6 changed TS files reported 6 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- **Check scripts, each exit 0:** `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-test-path-roots` and `check-phantom-dependencies`.

Declared narrowings:
- **Full `@object-ui/console` type-check: NOT MEASURED.** Its dependency closure is a build of the whole workspace. The one new file was checked, with a control, as above.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` type-check: NOT MEASURED.** The diff there is the content of one regex template literal and a comment, and its test program needs a 13-package closure build.
- **eslint narrowing:** `eslint.config.js` configures no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.

## Acceptance notes

- **An observation, not filed.** The console manifest tests describe the registry they load (`@object-ui/components` plus `src/register-plugins.ts`) as exactly the generators' read. That graph does not pass `assertFullyLoaded`: 8 blocks stay lazy stubs with no `inputs` (`markdown`, `object-calendar`, `object-chart`, `object-gantt`, `object-kanban`, `object-map`, `object-timeline`, `object-tree`). `dev/manifest-dump.tsx` adds 15 eager plugin imports to fill them in. The type count and the TS2430 were the same over both graphs, so this changes no reading here. The new pin avoids the question by running the dump itself.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/11075-every-node-declared-omit.md` declares `@object-ui/sdui-parser` `minor`.
